According to the Prophecy of Genesis, Chrysos Heirs are tasked with taking the Coreflames (the essence of their being, and taking it roughly the same as killing them in most cases) from the twelve Titans to usher in Era Nova, which is supposedly meant to be an era of paradise and peace. Mydeimos (Mydei) is the last prince of his nation, Castrum Kremnos, and obtained the Coreflame of Strife to become its demigod. His "flaw" is that he is immortal and returns to life if he is killed. Phainon is hailed as the future hero of Amphoreus as he's a Chrysos Heir without a "flaw", and Mydei calls him "Deliverer" for it.

The few times that he succeeded, all he did was meet Mydei’s unimpressed stare with a cheeky grin.

Even ravaged by disuse and time, the vaulted ceilings still shone with now-dulled mother of pearl murals and golden inlay in the shapes of waves and tilted chalices. The remnants of marble tables and once opulent-looking altars that were laden with wine and feasts in Eras past still stood in several places as they walked through the temple of the Ocean Titan and God of Banquets.

There really is not much here - well, not much besides some old, broken antique vases cast from oceanbed clay, tarnished silver utensils, old coins, and shattered plates with faded wave-like decorations around the edges. No light streams through the broken stained glass windows any more, not in the Evernight, nor does Phagousa’s presence permeate the temple beyond a faint, lingering echo.

Further into the temple are smaller chambers with faded murals growing darker and darker in color, as if mirroring the gradient from aqua to navy blue as you sink into the depths of the ocean. Little carved memorial plaques line the walls, their edges carved in the shapes of waves and coral, gilded and inlaid with gems and pearls. Mydei exchanges a quick glance with Phainon as they reach a stone door with some kind of glowing orb on the front, but neither of them sense danger - and so, they push onwards.

Mydei glances back at the dark blue wall, carvings of processions, parades, and celebrations flowing seamlessly over it in a way that makes it hard to tell that it was once an open doorway. Beside him, Phainon hums thoughtfully.

“I suppose the only way forward is through,” Phainon says lightly. When Mydei catches his eyes, Phainon just grins and shrugs. Mydei exhales - a little noise, not quite a laugh and not quite a scoff - and turns forward again.
